So `stateDiagram-V2` is a header. state.md#detection: The lexer then reads the header again, case-insensitively and followed by whitespace (see [The statement context](#the-statement-context)). So `stateDiagram-V2` is a header, while `stateDiagramX` and `stateDiagram-v3` are detected as state diagrams and rejected. The whitespace after the header may be a line break or not: a statement may follow the header on its line, and the header alone is accepted, also without a line feed after it, because the lexer reads a line feed after the last character (see [End of text](../common.md#end-of-text)).

patterns.comment: Rule 21: hide empty description, with exactly one space between words and a final word boundary, is the hide, empty and description-word units. state.md#the-statement-context: The words of rules 10 to 21 are compared case-insensitively, as everywhere in this diagram; the whitespace after them, line feeds included, belongs to no unit. The units `default`, `href` outside a click statement, `string` outside a click statement, and `invalid` are taken by no rule of the grammar, so an input with one of them is rejected.

state-direction.comment: TB, BT, RL and LR are tried in this order, at the last direction for that value; the surrounding runs are direction-text. directives inside direction-text join its parts; between direction and the value they are trivia. A directive is read whole, so its argument cannot supply direction or its value. Runs stop before separator-led common comments, and padding never consumes their separator. state.md#the-statement-context: **The direction line.** Compared case-insensitively: from the current position, a run of characters without line feeds, U+2028, or U+2029, the longest one that the rest can follow; then `direction`; then one or more whitespace characters; then one of `TB`, `BT`, `RL`, and `LR`, tried in this order; and then every character up to the next line feed. The rule reads `direction` as a `direction` unit, the value as a `direction-value` unit, and the characters before `direction` and after the value as `direction-text` units, which mermaid.js does not read. The rule is tried before the id rule, so it takes the whole line: `B : x direction LR` sets the direction and has no state, and so does `A --> B direction LR`, and `Direction lr` is a direction line. It is also tried before the comment rules, so the text after the value may hold `%%`: `direction LR %% c` sets the direction `LR`, and `%% c` is a `direction-text` unit, not a comment. Neither does the value need to end at a word boundary: `direction TBX` sets `TB`, and `X` is a `direction-text` unit. The values are tried in the order given: if the line has `direction`, whitespace, and `TB` anywhere, the value is `TB`; otherwise `BT` is tried, and so on. For a value, the lexer takes the last `direction` of the run that the value follows. So `direction TB x direction TB` is read at its last `direction`, and `direction TB x` is a `direction-text` unit, while `direction TB x direction LR` sets `TB` and is read at its first `direction`, with `x direction LR` as a `direction-text` unit. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.

patterns.comment: A double quote starts a string ending at the next double quote, with no escape mechanism. state.md#the-statement-context: - A directive starts at `%%{` only when zero or more whitespace characters and then a name, a word, follow it (see [Where a directive is](../common.md#where-a-directive-is)), and a comment starts at `%%` only when no `{` follows it. So `%%{}` and `%%{ }` are neither: their `%%` is an `ignored-text` unit, which the grammar takes only before the `{` of a body (see [Grammar](#composite-states-aliases-and-pseudostates)). `state X` followed by a line `%%{}`, `%%{ }`, or `%%{}%%` is the composite state X with an empty body, while after `A` the `{` is rejected; and after `state X`, a line `%%{init: {}}%%` or `%%{` followed by a line `A` is a directive, and `%% {}` is a comment, so X has no body.

state-comments.comment: Hash and percent-percent not followed by { start comments only at unit starts; ids consume an internal hash and end before an internal percent pair. Entities do not start hash comments. Native comment text ends before a separator-led common comment; neither percent of its mark may belong to a directive. state.md#comments: `#` and `%%` start a diagram comment where the comment rule of the current context is tried before a unit starts: at the start of a unit in the statement context, the composite body context, and the state context, and after an id and a `floating-note-id`, which end before a `%%` after their first character, and after an `alias-id`, which ends before any `%%`. After a `note-id`, the note text context has no comment rule. A comment after a statement is read so: `A --> B # c`, `A --> B %% c`, and `A --> B%% c` have the transition from A to B and a comment. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.

patterns.comment: An entity is converted before lexical reading and cannot start a hash comment. state.md#states-and-transitions: A state is written by its id, or as `[*]`, the start or the end. A `description` after a state is its description, and after a transition, the label of the transition. The second state of a transition is on the line of the arrow: `A -->`, a line break, and `B` is rejected.

patterns.comment: Read an empty string in the state context as ignored text. state.md#composite-states-aliases-and-pseudostates: So the empty strings are accepted wherever they lie in the state context, as in mermaid.js, and they change nothing in the Db.

Without a body the first colon separates the alias id and second-description; later colons belong to ignored text. A same-line body keeps the entire alias id. Multiline body lookahead is beyond the line-by-line limit. state.md#the-state-context: **The alias id context.** Zero or more characters other than line feed and `{` are an `alias-id` unit, without the whitespace at its ends; it ends before the first `%%`, also when that is its first character. It leaves the alias id context, so the state context reads on, where the `%%` starts a comment unless `{` follows. So the id after `as` may hold whitespace and `:`: `state "d" as my id` has the id `my id`, and the id may be empty: before a `{`, and before a `%%`, so that `state "d" as %% c` and `state "d" as %%A` are alias definitions with the empty id followed by a comment.

Keep colons inside a composite alias's id. state.md#the-state-context: The alias id is then not divided: `state "d" as A : x {`, and `state "d" as A : x` followed by a line `{`, define the composite state `A : x`, while after an empty line the `{` starts no body, and the input is rejected; a line of only whitespace, which rule 7 of the statement context reads with its line feed, makes no unit and changes nothing.

Divide only the first colon of an alias without a following body; directives and entity semicolons belong to text. state.md#the-state-context: **The alias id context.** Zero or more characters other than line feed and `{` are an `alias-id` unit, without the whitespace at its ends; it ends before the first `%%`, also when that is its first character. patterns.comment: Retain the suffix from the second colon as one ignored unit. state.md#the-state-context: When the alias statement has no body, the lexer divides the `alias-id` at its first `:`: the text before it is the `alias-id`, the `:` is a `:` unit, the text between it and the second `:`, or the end, is a `second-description` unit, which may be empty or all whitespace, and the text from the second `:` is an `ignored-text` unit, which mermaid.js does not read ([`stateDiagram.jison`](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/blob/1fb7869866dd619168d840291c9c54b4f129758b/packages/mermaid/src/diagrams/state/parser/stateDiagram.jison#L233-L243)). It has a body when a `{` follows the `alias-id`, on its line or after the line feed of its line and only line whitespace and comment lines, with only units between them that the grammar takes before the `{` of a body: empty description blocks, an `ignored-state` unit and empty strings, or a `%%` right before the `{` (see [Composite states, aliases, and pseudostates](#composite-states-aliases-and-pseudostates)). So `state "d" as A : x` followed by a line `%%{}` or `accDescr {} %%{}` defines the composite state `A : x` with an empty body.

So `state "d" as A : x` followed by a line `%%{}` or `accDescr {} %%{}` defines the composite state `A : x` with an empty body.

state-units.comment: Rules 22 to 26: terminals, ids, descriptions, transition arrows and class separators; ordinary ids are consumed without a scope to protect embedded keyword-like words. state.md#the-statement-context: The words of rules 10 to 21 are compared case-insensitively, as everywhere in this diagram; the whitespace after them, line feeds included, belongs to no unit. patterns.comment: An id is a maximal run excluding colon, whitespace, line feed, hyphen and {; internal percent pairs end it and internal hashes are characters. Ids have no added scope. state.md#units-and-contexts: **Ids.** In several contexts, the same rule reads an id: one or more characters other than `:`, line feed, whitespace, `-`, and `{`, as many as possible, makes an `id` unit. When the characters read contain `%%` after their first character, the unit ends before that `%%`, and the lexer reads on from the `%%` in the context that the rule leaves it in: in the statement, composite body, and state contexts, the `%%` starts a diagram comment (see [Comments](#comments)), while after a `note-id`, the note text context has no comment rule, and `note left of A%% c : hi` is rejected.

state-description.comment: Rule 24: colon introduces a description of non-colon/non-semicolon/non-line-feed characters or a colon followed by such a character; percent pairs, hashes and keywords are text. state.md#the-statement-context: **The direction line.** Compared case-insensitively: from the current position, a run of characters without line feeds, U+2028, or U+2029, the longest one that the rest can follow; then `direction`; then one or more whitespace characters; then one of `TB`, `BT`, `RL`, and `LR`, tried in this order; and then every character up to the next line feed. The rule reads `direction` as a `direction` unit, the value as a `direction-value` unit, and the characters before `direction` and after the value as `direction-text` units, which mermaid.js does not read. The rule is tried before the id rule, so it takes the whole line: `B : x direction LR` sets the direction and has no state, and so does `A --> B direction LR`, and `Direction lr` is a direction line. It is also tried before the comment rules, so the text after the value may hold `%%`: `direction LR %% c` sets the direction `LR`, and `%% c` is a `direction-text` unit, not a comment. Neither does the value need to end at a word boundary: `direction TBX` sets `TB`, and `X` is a `direction-text` unit. The values are tried in the order given: if the line has `direction`, whitespace, and `TB` anywhere, the value is `TB`; otherwise `BT` is tried, and so on. For a value, the lexer takes the last `direction` of the run that the value follows. So `direction TB x direction TB` is read at its last `direction`, and `direction TB x` is a `direction-text` unit, while `direction TB x direction LR` sets `TB` and is read at its first `direction`, with `x direction LR` as a `direction-text` unit.

state-note-line.comment: Note and whitespace, left or right, exactly one space, and of enter the note id context; an immediate percent run after of is ignored text. A colon after the id starts note text ending at colon, semicolon or line feed. Directives between these units are trivia. state.md#the-note-contexts: The keyword `left of` or `right of`, with one space between the words, the **position**: a `position` unit for `left` or `right` and an `of` unit; enters the note id context.

patterns.comment: The semicolon of an entity is part of note text. state.md#the-note-contexts: Zero or more whitespace, `as`, and zero or more whitespace: an `as` unit; leaves the context and enters the floating note id context.

state-note-block.comment: A positioned note reads the same header as a line note, then text through a line feed, whitespace and bounded end note with exactly one space. Directives next to that space lie between the end and note units. state.md#the-note-contexts: The **note id context** reads zero or more whitespace characters, line feeds included, and then an id of characters other than `:`, line feed, whitespace, and `-`: a `note-id` unit, which ends before the first `%%`, also when that is its first character, and is then empty. Without such a `%%`, it needs one or more characters: `note left of : x` is rejected.

state-accessibility-line.comment: Read the state-accessibility-line form. state.md#the-statement-context: - A directive starts at `%%{` only when zero or more whitespace characters and then a name, a word, follow it (see [Where a directive is](../common.md#where-a-directive-is)), and a comment starts at `%%` only when no `{` follows it. So `%%{}` and `%%{ }` are neither: their `%%` is an `ignored-text` unit, which the grammar takes only before the `{` of a body (see [Grammar](#composite-states-aliases-and-pseudostates)). `state X` followed by a line `%%{}`, `%%{ }`, or `%%{}%%` is the composite state X with an empty body, while after `A` the `{` is rejected; and after `state X`, a line `%%{init: {}}%%` or `%%{` followed by a line `A` is a directive, and `%% {}` is a comment, so X has no body. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.

Text and context variables below name the corresponding rules of this diagram. state.md#lexical-structure: The lexer of mermaid.js for this diagram compares letters case-insensitively (see [Notation](../common.md#notation)): `STATE A {`, `Note Left Of A : x`, and `HIDE EMPTY DESCRIPTION` are read as with the lower-case words. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.
